question: Can strong lottery tickets be stored more compactly by randomly fixing some source-network edges on and others off before optimizing the remaining binary supermask?

key_findings.claim: Partial freezing decouples supermask storage reduction from the ticket sparsity range by combining random pre-pruning with random locking.
key_findings.evidence: Pre-pruned weights are permanently absent and locked weights permanently present; only the remaining 1 minus freezing-ratio edges need optimized mask bits. Pruning sets the minimum attainable sparsity, while locking sets the maximum.

key_findings.claim: For a fixed freezing ratio, centering the unfrozen interval on the desired ticket sparsity maximizes candidate subnetworks and empirically works better with equal-edges-per-layer allocation than ERK.
key_findings.evidence: The derived heuristic sets pre-pruning to desired sparsity minus half the unfrozen proportion and locking to the remaining frozen proportion, clipped at zero; the Conv6 sweep reports EPL outperforming ERK across configurations.

key_findings.claim: A subset-sum extension gives an existence result for approximating arbitrary target ReLU networks inside sufficiently wide and one-layer-deeper frozen random networks.
key_findings.evidence: Lemmas 3.1-3.2 add Bernoulli locked and pruned terms to prior subset-sum arguments; Theorem 3.1 states high-probability SLT existence under uniform random weights and fixed per-layer pruning and locking ratios.

key_findings.claim: Freezing improves the reported accuracy-memory frontier across dense-optimum, sparse-optimum, and dense-ticket regimes.
key_findings.evidence: On CIFAR-10 Conv6, 40% mask reduction costs little accuracy and 70% costs about five points; frozen ResNet-18 still finds a 90%-sparse ticket with 88.1% accuracy after 90% mask reduction; frozen GIN retains 69.8% OGBN-Arxiv accuracy at 50% mask reduction versus 70.1% for the best dense-source ticket.

key_findings.claim: On ImageNet, freezing 70% of a ResNet source improves the size-accuracy trade-off over both dense-source and pruning-only strong-ticket searches.
key_findings.evidence: At fixed 80% ticket sparsity, frozen SKC ResNets give smaller or more accurate tickets; the abstract reports 3.3x compression relative to the dense-source SLT and up to 14.12 accuracy points over a similarly compressed random-pruning counterpart.

key_findings.claim: The compression benefit is currently a bit-count estimate, not measured hardware efficiency, and the theory does not prove locking is better than pruning.
key_findings.evidence: The limitations explicitly defer accelerator implementation, state the theorem only proves existence rather than comparative approximation superiority, leave optimal ratio theory open, and do not cover transformers.

method.core_idea: Randomly freeze a reproducible mixture of edges to zero and one so the learned binary supermask covers fewer parameters while remaining centered on the empirically useful ticket sparsity.
method.mechanism: Random weights, pruning masks, and locking masks are regenerated from seeds. Edge-Popup optimizes scores only for unfrozen edges; a ternary conceptual mask identifies off, optimized, and locked edges, but only the unfrozen binary choices and small metadata are stored.
assumptions: Random seeds and layer ratios can regenerate weights and frozen masks cheaply and deterministically on target hardware.
The desired strong-ticket sparsity is known or can be tuned without excessive search.
Optimizing fewer edge scores does not eliminate the useful ticket basin.
Bit-count reductions translate into lower off-chip traffic and end-to-end energy.

techniques.role: Permanently removes some edges and includes others before supermask optimization.
Positions the searchable interval around a desired ticket sparsity.
Optimizes edge scores and selects a globally fixed fraction without training weights.
Excludes random weights and frozen decisions from stored model bits.
Extends strong-ticket approximation theory to randomly locked and pruned sources.

evaluations.setting: Conv6 and ResNet-18 on CIFAR-10 plus four-layer GIN on OGBN-Arxiv, generally three repetitions.
evaluations.metric: Top-1 or node accuracy versus stored supermask memory across freezing and target sparsity.
evaluations.result: Appropriate pruning-locking mixtures match or improve dense- and sparse-source frontiers in all three optimal-sparsity regimes.
evaluations.baseline: Edge-Popup tickets in dense sources and random-pre-pruned sources.

evaluations.setting: Varying source width with Kaiming-uniform and signed-Kaiming-constant random weights.
evaluations.metric: Accuracy versus estimated bits for supermask plus batch-normalization parameters.
evaluations.result: Frozen-source tickets are as accurate or more accurate at similar or smaller memory; binary initialization helps most at narrower widths.
evaluations.baseline: Dense-source and pruning-only tickets at matched desired sparsity.

evaluations.setting: ResNet families on ImageNet at 80% ticket sparsity, one run per configuration.
evaluations.metric: Top-1 accuracy and estimated model storage.
evaluations.result: A 70%-frozen source yields a better reported frontier and large gains over high pre-pruning at matched storage.
evaluations.baseline: Weight training and SLTs found in dense or random-pruned ResNets.

limitations: Author-stated: actual specialized-hardware implementation and energy or latency measurements are future work.
Author-stated: the existence theorem does not prove freezing's approximation advantage over pruning-only sources.
Author-stated: there is no theoretical prescription for the optimal pruning-locking proportion.
Author-stated: transformer strong tickets are not established and are not evaluated.
ImageNet configurations have one run, limiting uncertainty estimates for a stochastic mask search.
failure_modes: Wrong target sparsity or freeze allocation can exclude the best tickets before search begins.
Locking too many harmful edges forces unavoidable interference; pruning too many induces layer collapse.
Seed regeneration and irregular sparse execution may cost more than saved off-chip memory on general hardware.
Edge-Popup may converge to different local mask optima, making single-run ImageNet gains unstable.
Batch-normalization parameters and metadata can dominate storage once masks become extremely compact.
reusable_insights: Use both fixed-zero and fixed-one random decisions to compress a combinatorial search without shifting its density range.
Center a reduced binary search interval around the desired cardinality to preserve the most candidate subsets.
Distinguish theoretical ticket existence, search success, stored bits, and realized hardware speed as separate claims.
Evaluate sparse-ticket methods across tasks whose best tickets are dense, intermediate, and highly sparse.
open_questions: Can pruning and locking ratios be predicted from architecture and data rather than tuned?
Do measured accelerator latency and energy follow the estimated mask-bit savings?
Can frozen strong tickets be found reliably in transformers or normalization-heavy models?
What landscape change makes moderate freezing sometimes improve search accuracy?

competitive_landscape.title: What's Hidden in a Randomly Weighted Neural Network?
competitive_landscape.relationship: Introduces Edge-Popup and strong tickets in dense random source networks.
competitive_landscape.difference: Ramanujan et al. optimize a full-source supermask; this paper freezes most mask decisions reproducibly to reduce stored bits while retaining the target density range.

competitive_landscape.title: Why Random Pruning Is All We Need to Start Sparse
competitive_landscape.relationship: Direct predecessor proving and finding strong tickets in randomly pre-pruned sources.
competitive_landscape.difference: Random pruning reduces mask storage but forces ticket sparsity above the pruning ratio; partial freezing adds fixed-on edges so compression no longer forces an excessively sparse ticket.

competitive_landscape.title: Proving the Lottery Ticket Hypothesis: Pruning Is All You Need
competitive_landscape.relationship: Foundational approximation theorem for subnetworks of random networks.
competitive_landscape.difference: Malach et al. prove dense-source existence; this paper extends the subset-sum proof template to sources with simultaneous random off and on constraints.

competitive_landscape.title: Pruning Untrained Neural Networks: Principles and Analysis
competitive_landscape.relationship: Competing initialization-time pruning analysis concerned with signal preservation and layer collapse.
competitive_landscape.difference: Pruning-at-initialization methods seek a trainable sparse network; frozen SLTs never train weights and optimize only a compact connectivity mask with some edges forced on.

novelty_assessment.author_claim: Randomly freezing both absent and present edges yields compact strong lottery tickets with better accuracy-memory trade-offs and retains a high-probability approximation guarantee.
novelty_assessment.reviewer_inference: Fixed-on randomness is a simple but genuinely useful extension of random-pre-pruned tickets because it decouples storage compression from sparsity. Empirical breadth is good, while hardware benefit, transformer transfer, and the reason locking improves search remain unresolved.

reviewer_notes: Read all 17 extracted pages, including construction, ratio heuristic, theorem and proof, every task regime, ImageNet table, limitations, and DeiT appendix. Direct arXiv and PMLR predecessors were checked on 2026-08-23.
